clue.text: Gallon cask housed by farmer for peat constituent

indicators.note: whatever is housed by something sits inside it, so the farmer word goes round the other pieces

blocks.note: a Boer is a South African farmer of Dutch descent
G is the standard abbreviation for gallon
a butt is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A farmer storing a gallon barrel of something useful for cutting peat.
explanation.walkthrough: BOG BUTTER is butter buried in peat bogs in casks long ago and later dug up, so the cask in the wordplay is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog butter is an ancient waxy deposit found buried in peat, so it is literally something the peat contains.

clue.text: Couch hostility before following shrink?

indicators.note: before places the hostility word ahead of the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: a couch is somewhere to lie, a bed
war is open hostility
F is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's couch and a patient's hostility, before the shrink follows up.
explanation.walkthrough: Couch and shrink set up a psychiatrist's session; 'shrink' is really the verb, make smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedwarf is to make dwarfish or stunted, so it means to make small; the question mark flags the pun on shrink.

clue.text: Carousal in Perth? Useless to grumble — drink up

indicators.note: read as use-less, it tells you to take the letters u, s, e out of the grumbling word
in a down clue up means the drink's letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to grouse is to complain or grumble
nog is a strong ale or an egg-nog

explanation.surface: A Scot at a party in Perth told it is pointless to complain and to drink up.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth looks Scottish, but it is the one in Western Australia: a grog-on is Australian slang. 'Useless' splits as use-less, GROUSE without USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grog-on is Australian slang for a drinking party, grog being their everyday word for alcohol, so it is a carousal.

clue.text: Drum and guitar's intro interrupting rock superstar

indicators.note: an intro is an opening, so only the first letter of guitar is used
a letter interrupting a name breaks into the middle of it

blocks.note: Bono is the lead singer of the rock band U2
the first letter of guitar

explanation.surface: A drum and the opening guitar riff break into a rock star's set.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is one of a pair of small hand-played drums of Latin American music.

clue.text: Water flow regulator, new, installed by complete duffer

indicators.note: a part installed by a fitter is put inside what the fitter is working on

blocks.note: a turkey is a complete flop or a useless person
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new valve fitted by an utterly incompetent plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: A turkey is slang for a dud, person or show.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey, like a turncock, is an old term for a valve or the official who turns water supply on and off.

clue.text: Work adequately matched rising rate

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to meet a standard is to match it adequately

explanation.surface: An appraisal of an employee whose output just about keeps pace with a rising pay rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or pace at which something happens, a synonym of rate.

clue.text: Those leading in the best type of rock

indicators.note: the leaders go in, inside the word for the best people

blocks.note: the elite are the best of a group
the van, the vanguard, is those at the front

explanation.surface: The top people in rock music lead the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rock music; the answer is a mineral. Elvan is a Cornish igneous rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvanite is elvan, a quartz-porphyry dyke rock found in Cornwall, so it names a kind of stone.

clue.text: The US take advantage of struggling pound, investing millions (6, two words)

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so these letters are muddled
to invest is to surround, as an army invests a town, so the letters enclose the millions

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Americans exploit a weak pound by investing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: The money surface hides a phrase: 'The US' marks it as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, to dump on someone is to treat them badly or exploit them, so it fits take advantage of.

clue.text: Golf course employee, one responsible for many extras?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who looks after the turf of a golf course
second meaning, punning: an inexperienced wicketkeeper lets through many byes

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are extras conceded when the wicketkeeper misses the ball, so a green (novice) keeper gives away many.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundsman of a golf course tends its putting surfaces, and the phrase splits into green, meaning inexperienced, plus keeper.

clue.text: Hitler's dream? He made list possibly

definitions.note: Herr is the German title for a man, the German counterpart of Mr

indicators.note: possibly says one set of letters could become another, so the two sides are rearrangements of the same pool

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the letters taken as written, removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Was someone who drew up a list fulfilling the Führer's wish?
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'He' stands in for the answer, and HERR plus MADE LIST rearranges to HITLER'S DREAM, so removing MADE LIST from that pool leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is how a German gentleman is styled, equivalent to Mister, so it stands for a male person, a he.

clue.text: Membrane or last of quinsy restricting part of throat, forming clots

indicators.note: restricting something confines it, so the membrane word holds the throat part
last of means only the final letter of quinsy is taken

blocks.note: a coat is a covering membrane or layer in anatomy
the gula is the upper part of the throat or gullet
taken as written
the final letter of quinsy

explanation.surface: A medical note about a throat infection affecting membranes and causing clotting.
explanation.walkthrough: Quinsy, a throat abscess, completes the medical picture but supplies just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coagulatory describes what causes or relates to coagulation, the thickening of blood into clots.

clue.text: A ruler, OE, excited when dressing queen in French cloak

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and do not keep their order
to dress something is to wrap clothing round it, so the stirred letters go around the royal piece

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
QU is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An Old English king gets worked up while putting his queen into a French cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual queen abbreviations ER and Q do not work here; Azed uses QU, which Chambers lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A roquelaure is an eighteenth-century knee-length cloak named after a French duke, the Duc de Roquelaure.

clue.text: Duvet to suffice covering one

blocks.note: 'that will do' means that will suffice
a thing on another covers it
a means one

explanation.surface: A duvet just about adequate to cover a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doona is the Australian everyday word, originally a trade name, for a quilt or continental quilt on a bed.

clue.text: End broken off, displace back bone, thin and flat

indicators.note: when the end breaks off a word it loses its final letter
going back means reading the shortened word from right to left

blocks.note: to displace something is to move it from its place

explanation.surface: An injury report: the tip snapped off and a bone was knocked out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back bone' looks like the spine, but 'back' is the reversal signal and 'bone' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The vomer is the thin flat plate of bone forming part of the partition between the nostrils.

clue.text: Estate car, lurid in colour but good to travel in

indicators.note: the travelling pieces go in, inside the word for the pale colour

blocks.note: lurid's older sense is pale and ghastly, that is wan
G is the abbreviation for good
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A garishly painted estate car that is still fine for a road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lurid' wants to mean gaudy here; its older sense, pale, is the one used. Waggon is the British double-g spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is called a station waggon, or simply a waggon, in North America and elsewhere.

clue.text: Spoil daily accepting money?

indicators.note: something that accepts another thing takes it in, so the newspaper word holds the cash letter

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Is a daily newspaper corrupted when it takes cash?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' could be a cleaning lady; here it is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper a person is to indulge them excessively, which is what spoiling a child means.

clue.text: No stranger to redundancy, among people on a strike

indicators.note: among says the answer sits within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of people, on, a and the start of strike

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with being laid off joins workers on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Redundancy suggests job losses; here it means needless repetition of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleonast habitually uses pleonasm, wordy repetition, so verbal redundancy is familiar to such a person.

clue.text: Bantus in pursuit stun African antelope

indicators.note: a thing in pursuit comes after, so the Bantu people are placed behind the knockout

blocks.note: KO, a knockout, stuns an opponent
the Ngoni are a Bantu people of southern Africa

explanation.surface: Tribesmen chase and knock out an antelope on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hunt, but the Bantus are simply named by one of their peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: The kongoni is the Coke's hartebeest, a large antelope of East African grassland.

clue.text: After single, member of gang possibly returns to crease

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the animal is read backwards

blocks.note: in cricket a single is one run
a gang is a collective noun for elk

explanation.surface: A batsman takes a single and gets back to the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'crease' the batting line; it is really a verb. A gang of elk is a collective noun. Runkle is Scots for to wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: To runkle is a Scots and northern word meaning to wrinkle or crumple, so it is a synonym of crease.

clue.text: Place for a drink and what that might be with German ignoring queue?

blocks.note: a bar is where drinks are served
the drink might be gin
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German at the bar jumps the queue for his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' refers back to the drink, which might be gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Barging in means pushing rudely forward, which is what someone does when they jump a queue.

clue.text: Aussie drunk, very smelly, no saint

indicators.note: no saint means the saint's abbreviation is taken away

blocks.note: stinky means very smelly
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: An unflattering description of a reeking Australian drunkard who is no saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky is Australian slang for intoxicated, recorded in Chambers as a colloquial adjective.

clue.text: River diverted, lake's dry wretchedly, refreshed liquidly no longer

indicators.note: a diverted river is sent elsewhere, so its letter leaves the fodder
wretchedly suggests a state of disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A river was diverted and the lake ran dry, a sorry state for those who drank from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an archaic form: the Y- prefix is the old past participle marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Yslaked is an obsolete past participle of slake, to quench thirst, so it means refreshed by drink.

clue.text: What trappers were after, left to prepare traps?

indicators.note: a word that traps another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: to fix a meal is to prepare it
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fur trapper's instructions: the left-hand man sets the snares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' looks like part of the definition's picture, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flix is an old word for fur or beaver down, the pelt that fur trappers hunted animals for.

clue.text: Travel lodge? Maria singularly takes refuge in it

indicators.note: one who takes refuge in a place goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
maria are the dark plains on the Moon; one of them is a mare

explanation.surface: A woman called Maria shelters alone in a motorway hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria reads as a woman's name; it is the plural of the Latin mare, a lunar sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaret is a Turkish hospice or inn where pilgrims and travellers could lodge, hence the question mark.

clue.text: No longer together, son makes up for shortcomings

blocks.note: atone is an obsolete adverb meaning at one, in agreement
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son of a broken marriage tries to compensate for his parents' failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete sense: atone once meant at one, together.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, so someone who atones is compensating for wrongs or failings.

clue.text: Carter's lad travellin' northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue going northwards means the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: repping, working as a travelling sales representative, with its g dropped like the clue's

explanation.surface: A carter's boy speaking dialect on his way up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the clue signals the dropped g in the wordplay word too.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipper was a carter's or carrier's boy who helped on rounds, as well as a general term for a young lad.

clue.text: Rich embroidery (not new) winding round old pulpit

indicators.note: not new means the abbreviation for new is dropped from the word
going round something means enclosing it

blocks.note: a winding is a turn in a road or river
an ambo is a raised pulpit in early churches

explanation.surface: Ornate needlework wrapped around an ancient pulpit as a church decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' looks like the anagram signal; it is the noun turn, which loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tambour is embroidery worked on a drum-shaped frame of that name, a fine decorative needlework.

clue.text: Lichen: Nebraska's where you'll find it

indicators.note: saying where a state is found puts its abbreviation inside the country

blocks.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for Nebraska
Nebraska is in the USA

explanation.surface: A note on where a particular lichen grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The geography of the clue is literal: Nebraska is inside the USA, and so are its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Usnea is a genus of beard lichen, grey-green tufts hanging from tree branches.

clue.text: Mountain pass the Scots have found captivating you and me

indicators.note: to captivate is to take captive, holding something within

blocks.note: hae is the Scots form of have
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A Highland pass that two visitors find enchanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hause, or hawse, is a Scots and northern English word for a narrow neck of land or col between hills.

clue.text: Foxing well-known septet maybe interrupted by cheers

indicators.note: a word interrupted by another has that other word break into its middle

blocks.note: the seven deadly sins are a famous group of seven
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A famous group of seven musicians baffled by heckling cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxing' reads as puzzling, but it is the noun for brownish spots on old paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxing is the reddish-brown spotting that discolours old books and prints, that is marks or blemishes on the page.

clue.text: Monkey dropping in for palm cereal

indicators.note: dropping the word in means it falls out of the monkey's name

blocks.note: a sagoin is a South American marmoset
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey drops by to steal palm-based breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is the starchy food extracted from the pith of the sago palm, eaten as a grain-like pudding.

clue.text: Spirit in bottle causing endless dismay after good rub initially

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of rub is kept
endless means the final letter of dismay's synonym is cut

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the first letter of rub
to appal is to fill with dismay

explanation.surface: A genie released from a bottle by rubbing, to the dismay of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The bottle and the rub suggest a genie; the spirit is actually a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pressings, a strong alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: One old tar capsizing major vessel

indicators.note: a capsizing boat throws everything about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a means one
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor overturning a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailing surface makes 'vessel' a ship; it is a blood vessel. Tar is a sailor too, but here the word is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Tent erected in wood (no one inside)

indicators.note: no here means the word for one is removed from the timber
the upright piece goes in, inside the shortened timber

blocks.note: teak is a hardwood
a means one
something erected is put up

explanation.surface: A tent pitched in a forest with nobody inside.
explanation.walkthrough: '(No one inside)' says the A for one is taken from inside the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A tupek is an Inuit summer tent made of animal skins.

clue.text: Convert from granite a form of Eire gneiss

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A geologist on how granite is transformed into an Irish gneiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Gneiss looks like part of the geology; it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Greisen is a rock formed by altering granite, so to greisenise is to change granite into greisen.

clue.text: Ancient earthwork in original condition? One's amazed

indicators.note: the earthwork is placed in, inside the word for the state

blocks.note: sted is an old spelling of stead, place or state
an agger is a Roman earthen rampart or raised road

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finding a Roman embankment intact is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: An agger is the raised embankment of a Roman road or rampart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staggered is so astonished that they are thrown off balance, an idiom for amazement.
